investigator.note: I prioritized earthquakes due to their extreme severity and recent catastrophic impact on Antakya (including the 2023 M7.8 and M6.3 earthquakes), as well as extreme rainfall given the history of daily precipitation exceeding 110 mm, alongside minor fire and industrial risks. For earthquake readiness, I assessed access to open ground for emergency evacuation, hospital proximity, general building density, and veterinary care facilities. For flood exposure, I analyzed low-lying block distribution, vulnerable schools and hospitals in flood-prone zones, flood refuge availability, and natural land cover changes between 2016 and 2025. Additionally, I screened industrial site proximity to measure chemical and fire risk exposure.

events.what_happened: A catastrophic 7.8-magnitude earthquake struck southern Turkey, causing widespread building collapses and killing tens of thousands of people in Antakya.
Massive wildfires swept across Hatay province, injuring at least 10 people and forcing widespread evacuations of residential areas.
An oil slick originating from a power plant leak in Syria reached the southern coast of Hatay, threatening local marine ecosystems and fisheries.
Extreme summer heatwaves with temperatures reaching 36°C severely exacerbated living conditions for earthquake survivors residing in temporary tent and container cities.
Heavy torrential rainfall triggered severe flooding and a landslide in Antakya that killed three people, destroyed homes, and swept away infrastructure.

report.area: Antakya, Hatay, Turkey (centre 36.2037, 36.1638, radius 1500 m, 73 blocks)
report.summary: Antakya faces significant risks from high seismic activity and severe rainfall, having experienced a magnitude 7.8 earthquake on 2023-02-06 and single-day rainfall up to 115 mm on 2003-12-08. Readiness is mixed: while 86.7% of residents are within 500 m of open ground for earthquake evacuation, 42,007 residents in flood-prone blocks lack a flood refuge within 300 m. Priority must be given to establishing flood refuges and improving emergency access near vulnerable sites.

calamities.what_happened: Magnitude 7.8 earthquake, 137 km from this place (Pazarcik earthquake, Kahramanmaras earthquake sequence); depth 10 km.
Magnitude 6.3 earthquake, 13 km from this place (2 km NNW of Uzunba?, Turkey); depth 16 km.
115 mm of rain in one day at this location (CHIRPS satellite-gauge estimate).

readiness.why_it_matters_here: Antakya is highly active seismically, experiencing 11 earthquakes of magnitude 5.5 or more within 200 km since 1970, including the catastrophic M7.8 and M6.3 events in February 2023.

matrix.finding: Only 4.5% of residents are within 500 m of a major hospital and 21.3% within 1000 m; median walk distance is 1687 m.
86.7% of residents are within 500 m of open ground (69 open grounds mapped), with a median walk distance of 236 m.
0.0% of residents are within 500 m of veterinary care, with a median walk distance of 2735 m. No animal shelter or zoo is mapped within 3 km.
Built area share decreased from 81.2% in 2016 to 77.7% in 2025, while bare land increased from 0.1% to 4.2%. Tree cover stands at 14.0%.

readiness.why_it_matters_here: Historical satellite records show single-day extreme rainfall events reaching up to 115 mm on 2003-12-08 and 99 mm on 2011-12-08.

matrix.finding: 43 out of 73 blocks (58.9%) are low-lying/flood-prone, containing 53,953 residents. 15 vulnerable sites including Özel Antakya Göz Hastanesi and Hatay Erol Bilecik Mesleki ve Teknik Anadolu Lisesi are in flood-prone blocks.
35 flood-prone blocks housing 42,007 residents lack a flood refuge within 300 m. There are 9 underpass segments prone to flooding.
Water cover share dropped from 0.2% in 2016 to 0.1% in 2025. Tree cover decreased from 15.3% to 14.0%.

recommendations.what: Designate and construct accessible elevated flood refuges or shelters in unequipped low-lying blocks.
recommendations.where: Gap hexes including 892da16601bffff, 892da166093ffff, and 892da16643bffff across low-lying districts.
recommendations.why: 35 flood-prone blocks housing 42,007 residents currently lack a flood refuge within a 300 m walk.

recommendations.what: Implement localized flood barriers and specialized emergency evacuation plans for critical health and educational infrastructure.
recommendations.where: Özel Antakya Göz Hastanesi, Hatay Erol Bilecik Mesleki ve Teknik Anadolu Lisesi, Cemalettin Tınaztepe Ortaokulu, and Atatürk İlköğretim Okulu.
recommendations.why: 1 hospital and 14 school facilities are situated within low-lying, flood-prone blocks.

recommendations.what: Improve medical transit routes and emergency access to major hospital infrastructure.
recommendations.where: General Şükrü Kanatlı (hex 892da16642bffff), Hacı Ömer Alpagot (hex 892da166013ffff), and Küçükdalyan (hex 892da166083ffff).
recommendations.why: Only 4.5% of residents live within 500 m of a major hospital, and worst-served blocks face walk distances up to 3212 m.
